recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future work should not duplicate FHIR-17424 prose unless OO makes a new decision; the cardinality request is already correctly represented in the active source.
issue_request: FHIR-17424 asked OO to make Specimen.subject optional because valid specimen-processing systems may track a specimen without knowing or caring who or what the subject is; the final resolution was to change Specimen.subject to 0..1.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit d79e04233833eb6ffcc1b5f40ee816ff09a3a8c1, titled "GF#17424 change specimen.subject to 0..1", which changed the historical Specimen spreadsheet subject row from 1..1 to 0..1 before later source refactoring moved the active definition into source/specimen/structuredefinition-Specimen.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists specimen=Specimen, so the current Specimen StructureDefinition is build-scope source. Later applied Specimen issues FHIR-53384 and FHIR-56301 revised subject/focus semantics for R6, including adding Specimen.focus and updating the subject-of-record wording, but they did not reverse the optional Specimen.subject cardinality.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because source/specimen/structuredefinition-Specimen.xml currently defines Specimen.subject with min value 0 and max value 1.
